subject: opening remote R session from a local instance of VIM

messages.author: a10a6a25f763d15f
messages.subject: opening remote R session from a local instance of VIM
parts:
Hello Dear List.

I am fairly new to the vim-r-plugin. What I have been trying to do is starting a R session on a remote server (via ssh for example) and using local instance of vim to send commands to that session. I can manage to send commands (via vim screen plugin), but I am not able to get feedback from R session.

For a while I thought that maybe it's not possible (or at least not that easy) but I came upon a certain website: http://manuals.bioinformatics.ucr.edu/home/programming-in-r/vim-r

The author there repeatedly says that it's in fact possible to make remote R session and local vim communicate:

"Flexible code sending options from local vim instances to R sessions on remote machines or among remote machines"

"The vim session can run on a local computer, while the R session can run on the same or a remote system."

However nowhere in that document is it mentioned how can one achieve this exactly.

So I would like to ask: is it possible? (for me that would be grand)

Warm Regards,
Karolis K.

messages.author: b256a2742aacd200
messages.subject: Re: opening remote R session from a local instance of VIM
parts:
Did you follow the instructions in http://www.lepem.ufc.br/jaa/r-plugin.html#r-plugin-remote ?

You can not send commands from the local machine to the remote machine. You can access the remote machine through ssh and, then, start tmux, vim and R in the remote machine. I will change the documentation to make this more clear.

Note that is better do not run Tmux in the local machine because Tmux environment variables could be passed to the remote machine and make the plugin confuse.

messages.author: b256a2742aacd200
messages.subject: Re: opening remote R session from a local instance of VIM
parts:
If you install the screen.vim plugin (http://www.vim.org/scripts/script.php?script_id=2711), you can do the following:

  1. Start Vim in a terminal emulator. (or even better, start either Tmux or Screen and then start Vim, depending on how your screen.vim is configured).

  2. Use the screen.vim plugin command to split the window and run bash.

  3. In the new split window, ssh to the remote machine and start R there.

  4. Use the screen.vim command (:ScreenSend) to send lines from local Vim to remote R through ssh.

Note, however, that this is no longer the Vim-R-plugin because none of its features will be available. With the above procedure, the communication between Vim and R is limited to sending lines of code already written in Vim to R Console through Tmux+ssh.

The communication between Vim-R-plugin and R is more complete. It has 3 channels:

  1. Code from Vim to R console.
  2. Messages from Vim to vimcom server running in R.
  3. Messages from vimcom to Vim server.

Moreover, the Vim-R-plugin (like Tinn-R) generates code that is sent either to R Console or to vimcom. The code generated under user request and is used to help writing the script, but should not be in the script itself, like help(), print(), args(), ls(), setwd(), knitr(), etc.
